scope: Theorem 6.3 (Tested transport) of the manuscript “Virasoro Constraints for Projective Complete Intersections” (preprints/Virasoro-Constraints-for-Projective-Complete-Intersections-September-24-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 065 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 01a2df978a0bfae2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 33-34. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider either configuration of Theorem 6.1, with the coherent admissible singles and degree data just specified. Suppose that all three short target types satisfy the 33 absolute Virasoro constraints in every genus, every curve class, and with all cohomology insertions. Then, for every k > 0, every finite number s of independent replicas, and every admissible test T, all coefficients of T (L (1) k,XZ (1) X ) ⊗ s O r=2 Z (r) X ! (6.3) vanish, where X is the main smooth target. The coefficients are selected by the coherent degree data, with the final exceptional degrees retained in the blowup configuration. The operator acts only on replica 1, before the test is applied.
